questions.question: A student burns a food sample to heat 50 g of water. Which equation is used to calculate the energy provided by the food in Joules (J)?
options: Energy (J) = mass of water (g) x rise in temperature (°C) x 4.2
Energy (J) = mass of water (g) + rise in temperature (°C) x 4.2
Energy (J) = mass of water (g) x rise in temperature (°C) / 4.2
Energy (J) = mass of water (g) / rise in temperature (°C) x 4.2

questions.question: Which two physical measurements of an individual are required to calculate their Body Mass Index (BMI)?
options: Waist circumference and body mass
Height and body mass
Age and height
Height and waist circumference

questions.question: Which of the following health issues is a person who is obese at an increased risk of developing?
options: Scurvy
Heart disease
Iron deficiency anaemia
Rickets

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'recovery time' after a person completes a physical exercise?
options: The time it takes to complete a specific fitness activity
The time taken for the breathing rate to double during a workout
The time it takes for the heart rate to return to its resting rate
The total duration of sleep required after high-intensity exercise

questions.question: How does a person's level of physical fitness generally affect their recovery time after exercise?
options: Fitter people have a longer recovery time.
Fitter people have a shorter recovery time.
Fitness level has no effect on recovery time.
Fitter people never have their heart rate return to resting level.

questions.question: In an investigation comparing the effect of different exercises on heart rate, which of the following are control variables?
options: The type of exercise and the final heart rate
The person being tested and the length of time spent exercising
The starting heart rate and the independent variable
The room temperature and the recovery time only

questions.question: When plotting a bar chart to show how different categories of exercise affect heart rate, where should the independent variable be placed?
options: On the x-axis
On the y-axis
In the chart legend only
On both the x-axis and y-axis

questions.question: Why do breathing rate and heart rate increase during exercise?
options: To reduce the amount of water vapor in the lungs
To deliver more oxygen to cells for cellular respiration
To decrease the body temperature of active muscles
To store extra carbon dioxide within the muscle tissues

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only valid major food groups needed by the human body?
options: Protein, carbohydrate, lipids/fats, water, minerals, vitamins, fibre
Protein, carbon dioxide, oxygen, water, minerals, vitamins
Carbohydrate, sugar, glucose, starch, fibre, water, calcium
Lipids/fats, protein, amino acids, minerals, vitamins, oxygen

questions.question: Why might an active teenager require a different daily intake of nutrients compared to an elderly person with a sedentary lifestyle?
options: Nutrient requirements are identical for all humans regardless of age or activity.
People need different amounts of particular nutrients at different times in their lives, depending on their lifestyle.
Teenagers only require vitamins, while elderly people only require proteins.
Sedentary people require more carbohydrates to sustain their daily activities.

questions.question: In a school laboratory experiment to compare the energy content of different foods, how is the energy released from the food directly measured?
options: By measuring the volume of gas produced when the food decays
By burning the food to heat water and measuring the temperature change
By dissolving the food in acid and measuring the change in pH
By weighing the food before and after it is left in sunlight

questions.question: Besides providing materials for growth and repair, what is another vital function of food in the human body?
options: It acts as an inert filler to keep the digestive tract permanently full.
It provides the fuel for cellular respiration, to provide energy for life processes.
It is converted directly into carbon dioxide to be stored in the bones.
It is used by the lungs to filter incoming oxygen from the air.

questions.question: Which two units of measurement are commonly used on food packaging to compare the amount of energy provided by food?
options: Grams and milliliters
Kilojoules and calories
Watts and Newtons
Degrees Celsius and Joules per gram

questions.question: Which of the following can be interpreted as symptoms of ill health in an individual?
options: Constant high physical fitness and high energy levels
Maintaining a stable, healthy body mass index
Changes in normal body appearance, function and behaviour
Having a normal resting heart rate of 70 beats per minute

questions.question: What is the primary cause of a deficiency disease in humans?
options: Consuming a diet that contains too many calories
Not consuming enough of a particular nutrient
Exercising too intensely without adequate rest periods
Exposure to harmful bacteria in drinking water

questions.question: How can a person's heart rate in beats per minute (bpm) be measured?
options: By counting their breathing rate per minute
By taking a person's pulse
By measuring their body temperature with a thermometer
By calculating their total energy intake in kilojoules
